core_obligations: Produce the polynomial coefficients (proof lines 14531-14544): from a^n congruent to 1 mod bA, build a_1, ..., a_n in A successively so that 1 = a^n + a_1 a^{n-1} b + a_2 a^{n-2} b^2 + ... + a_n b^n, using at each stage the unit property of a^{n-i} modulo bA and the fact that the running remainder lies in b^{i}A.
Form the monogenic extension (proof lines 14547-14550): set B = A[y]/(y^n + a_1 y^{n-1} + ... + a_n).

Show u = a - by is a unit by the prime-ideal argument (proof lines 14551-14563): if a prime q of B over p contained u, then either b is in p, which is impossible since then a is not in p and u is a unit modulo p, or b is not in q, in which case y mod q equals a/b mod q and the defining relation becomes b^{-n} = 0 in B/q, a contradiction.
Conclude that the constructed B and y satisfy the statement (proof lines 14562-14563).
proof_roadmap: From the root-of-unity hypothesis, build the coefficients a_i by successive division, so that the polynomial y^n + a_1 y^{n-1} + ... + a_n is monogenic over A.
Assume a prime q of B over p contains a - by and split on whether b lies in p.
If b is in p then a is not, so a - by is a unit modulo q; if b is not in q then y = a/b in B/q and the defining relation gives b^{-n} = 0, a contradiction.
Hence a - by is a unit in B.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a monogenic extension A subset B in which a Bezout pair (a, b) with a mod bA of finite multiplicative order becomes a unit u = a - by (statement lines 14522-14528). There are two genuinely separate constructions: first the coefficients a_1, ..., a_n are manufactured by an explicit successive-division argument from a^n congruent to 1 mod bA (proof lines 14531-14544), which is where the root-of-unity hypothesis is consumed; then the resulting polynomial y^n + a_1 y^{n-1} + ... + a_n defines B = A[y]/(f), and u is shown to be a unit by a prime-ideal argument that splits on whether b lies in the prime below (proof lines 14551-14563), the contradiction in the second case coming from the very identity built in the first step. The claim is H2: two explicit constructions, each short but neither formal.
